parsed.why: No facility ban or criminal exposure; hate-crime law covers gender identity. Strict surgical marker rules and care bans are resident-facing. Slightly above parent average.
Adds facility restriction in state-run buildings and schools, no GI hate-crime or non-discrimination coverage, and possible solitary confinement for detained trans people. Below parent.
Documented mob attack with victims charged, no attacker arrested, hospital denial, men's jail and male guard search despite female ID. State response damning; worse than parent.
Bathroom-bounty law reaches public buildings including airports, with private lawsuits and invalidated licences. Universal exposure with no working remedy; well below parent.
Criminal bathroom law reaches private businesses and hospitals, up to one year jail per offence, steeper than any other. Most severe universal exposure; lowest score.
